comments.note: runPersonaPartials in src/plugins/runner.ts (line 193) does not guard against a plugin returning null/undefined — if a misbehaving plugin returns null, the accumulated map becomes null and downstream resolvePartials would throw. This is consistent with how runPartials is implemented, so it is a pre-existing pattern rather than a new defect. A defensive `?? accumulated` fallback would harden the runner. Not a blocker for this WP.

The shallow copy ({ ...partialsMap }) is correctly placed in buildPersona() before calling runPersonaPartials, ensuring each persona starts from the unmodified suite-level map. No issues with the isolation strategy.

comments.note: Renamed fractional step label '3.5' → '3b' in the buildPersona() JSDoc pipeline comment (line 367) and inline section banner (line 436) in src/builders/persona-builder.ts. The integer-based step numbering convention (1–12) is used throughout the function; a decimal sub-step is inconsistent. '3b' is more conventional and avoids confusion with a float literal. No behavior change — documentation only.

runPersonaPartials (src/plugins/runner.ts, line 193) lacks a null/undefined guard on plugin return values. If a plugin returns null, `accumulated` becomes null and downstream resolvePartials will throw at runtime. This is a pre-existing pattern consistent with runPartials and runBuildContext runners. A defensive `?? accumulated` fallback (i.e., `accumulated = plugin.onPersonaPartials(...) ?? accumulated`) would silently skip malformed plugins rather than crashing. Recommended as a follow-up hardening task across all runners, not specific to this WP.

The partialsMap parameter of buildPersona() is only ever used to seed the shallow copy ({ ...partialsMap }) passed to runPersonaPartials; it is never forwarded to rendering directly. A future rename to suitePartialsMap would make the call-site intent clearer (caller provides the suite-level map; persona-level map is the result). No urgency — the current name is not wrong, just less expressive post-WP-005.

[documentation-forward] The buildPersona() JSDoc @param for partialsMap (line 386–387) describes it as 'Pre-loaded partials map (shared + suite-local merged)' but does not mention that it serves as the base for onPersonaPartials persona-scoped overrides. The documentation should clarify that this map is shallow-copied before being passed to the onPersonaPartials hook and that the hook's output — not this parameter — is what reaches resolvePartials.

[documentation-forward] The plugin interface documentation (wherever PersonaBuildPlugin.onPersonaPartials is described) should document the shallow-copy isolation guarantee: callers must not mutate the input map directly; they should return a new map. The test suite demonstrates the correct pattern (spread + merge) but the interface contract itself should state this explicitly.
